start_here: Say to your AI: "Use gallery-dl on my computer: download the images, videos and post details of a public profile, gallery or post from a web address such as Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest or Reddit, with https://example.com/user/demo-profile." It reads the row, installs gallery-dl if it is missing, runs it and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: gallery-dl is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on what it is handed there.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use gallery-dl on my computer: download the images, videos and post details of a public profile, gallery or post from a web address such as Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest or Reddit, with https://example.com/user/demo-profile." It reads the row with do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:mikf-gallery-dl"}.
2. It checks that python are on your computer, and if gallery-dl is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/mikf/gallery-dl.git ; python -m pip install -U gallery-dl.
3. It runs the row's command: gallery-dl https://example.com/user/demo-profile
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. The site you asked through runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: gallery-dl: the posts of a public profile at example.com
worked_examples.ask: Use gallery-dl on my computer: download the images, videos and post details of a public profile, gallery or post from a web address such as Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest or Reddit, with https://example.com/user/demo-profile.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json: tool:github:mikf-gallery-dl runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got gallery-dl in, the command line: gallery-dl https://example.com/user/demo-profile
worked_examples.hands_back: gallery-dl prints one line per file it saves ("./gallery-dl/example/demo-profile/1001_01.jpg") and leaves the profile's images and videos, with each post's details beside them when asked with --write-metadata, in a gallery-dl folder where it ran.
